cities.name: Chicago

probateCourt.name: Circuit Court of Cook County, County Department, Probate Division
probateCourt.address: Richard J. Daley Center, 50 West Washington St., Room 1202, Chicago, IL 60602

localNotes: Cook County probate cases are handled by the Probate Division of the Circuit Court, with the clerk's main probate office in Room 1202 of the Richard J. Daley Center, 50 West Washington Street, Chicago. Probate case documents are filed electronically through eFile Illinois (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

A will can be filed with the Probate Division in person at the Daley Center, by mail to the Daley Center, or in person at any of the clerk's five branch offices. The clerk lists no fee for filing a will (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

The Cook County Clerk of the Circuit Court lists a Pro Se/Self-Represented Litigant Center and a guide to free and low-cost legal services in Cook County on its probate page (source: https://www.cookcountyclerkofcourt.org/divisions/probate-division).

Cook County's recorder of deeds is the Cook County Clerk's Recordings office (312.603.3974). The Clerk's Property After Death resource guide describes the Illinois Transfer on Death Instrument as a single document that moves a home at death, and points to the Clerk's forms page (source: https://cookcountyclerkil.gov/publications/property-after-death-resource-guide). Confirm the recording requirements for your instrument with that office or an attorney.

probateCourt.address: 505 N. County Farm Rd., Wheaton, IL 60187

localNotes: DuPage County's court probate and guardianship page lists the Circuit Court Clerk's Office on the first floor of the courthouse at 505 N. County Farm Rd., Wheaton (630-407-8700), and says guardian reports are e-filed through i2file (source: https://www.dupagecourts.gov/18th_judicial_circuit_court/probate___guardianship/).

The DuPage County Recorder is at 421 N. County Farm Road, Wheaton, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, and accepts documents in person or by mail. This is the office that records a deed or transfer on death instrument for DuPage property (source: https://www.dupageco.org/recorder/).

The DuPage circuit clerk's filing fee book lists no fee to file a will, and a $300 fee to open a decedent's estate, in the schedule effective September 11, 2026. Fees change, so check the current book (source: https://dupagecircuitclerk.gov/18thJudicial/viewstaticpdf?pdfFile=FilingFeesSchedule.pdf).

probateCourt.address: Lake County Courthouse, 18 N. County St., Waukegan, IL 60085

localNotes: Lake County's probate court sits in the main courthouse at 18 N. County St., Waukegan; the Probate Division's phone is 847-377-3260 (source: https://www.19thcircuitcourt.state.il.us/1331/Probate-Court).

The Lake County probate standing order effective January 12, 2026 requires attorneys and parties to e-file with the Circuit Clerk, and sets hearing days by case type, including Wednesdays for adult guardianships and Fridays for self-represented litigants (source: https://19thcircuitcourt.state.il.us/DocumentCenter/View/5887/DJV-Standing-Order---Procedures-for-Probate-Guardianship-Division-Cases---1-12-26).

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division is at 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan (847-377-2575, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays). Its deed-recording checklist includes any local municipal transfer tax stamp, which must be obtained before submitting a deed (sources: https://www.lakecountyil.gov/Faq.aspx?QID=558 and https://www.lakecountyil.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3233/Pamphlet---Recording-Deeds-PDF).

cities.name: Batavia
localNotes: The Batavia Township Assessor's office is at 201 Houston Street, Suite 300, phone (630) 879-1323, open Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, email assessor@bataviatownship.com. (source: https://www.bataviatownship.com/?p=155)

Batavia Township's community links list Senior Services Associates (Illinois Community Care Program), Ride In Kane for riders 65 and older, and township General Assistance; the township phone is (630) 879-1392. (source: https://www.bataviatownship.com/community-links/)

The Batavia Park District runs senior programs for ages 50+ and the Batavia Senior Citizens Club, which meets monthly on the third Wednesday. Recreation contact is 630-239-0999 ext. 2064; the district is at 327 West Wilson Street. (source: https://bataviaparks.org/program/social-senior-programs/)

cities.name: Lake Forest
localNotes: Lake Forest's Dickinson Hall Senior Center has a Senior Advocate, Janet Fryer, who gives free, confidential help by phone, at the hall or at home with Medicare, the Benefit Access Program and Senior Citizen's Assessment Freeze applications. Call 847-810-4678. (source: https://cityoflakeforest.com/community/dickinson_hall/services/)

Shields Township covers Lake Forest north of Route 60 and lists assistance for seniors and low-income residents plus property tax appeal and relief pages. The office is at 906 West Muir Avenue, Lake Bluff, 847-234-0802; the part of Lake Forest south of Route 60 is not in Shields Township. (source: https://www.shieldstownship.com/community/index.php)

Lake County's senior homestead exemption reduces equalized assessed value by $8,000 for owners 65 or older who live in the home. It does not need yearly renewal, and a new parcel number means a new application; the Chief County Assessment Office help line is 847-377-2100. (source: https://www.lakecountyil.gov/457/Senior-Homestead-Exemption)

Lake County probate petitions must be filed by an attorney, and the original will must be filed within 30 days after death at a Lake County Circuit Clerk office. Probate court dates are Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays at 9:00 AM. (source: https://www.lakecountycircuitclerk.org/201/Wills-Probate)

cities.name: Libertyville
localNotes: The Libertyville Township Assessor's office is at 359 Merrill Court, Libertyville, 847-362-5900, open Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. It lists homestead, senior, senior freeze and home improvement exemptions and helps seniors file for the senior homestead exemption. (source: https://libertyvilletownship.us/about-us/assessor)

cities.name: Mundelein
localNotes: Fremont Township Senior Services, 22385 W. Route 60, Mundelein, 847-223-2847, is open 8:30 to 3:30 Monday through Friday. It offers a free SHIP Medicare counselor, Benefit Access applications, reduced-fare transit passes and Community Care Program referrals. (source: https://fremonttownship.com/?p=488)
The Fremont Township Assessor's Office helps seniors apply for homestead exemptions and can be reached at 847-223-2846. (source: https://fremonttownship.com/?p=488)

The Lake County Circuit Clerk lists a Mundelein branch at 105 E Route 83, Mundelein, 847-377-3300; the page does not say which matters that branch handles, so confirm before bringing a will. The main branch is at 18 N. County Street, Waukegan, 847-377-3380. (source: https://www.lakecountycircuitclerk.org/201/Wills-Probate)

cities.name: Gurnee
localNotes: The Warren Township Senior Center serves Gurnee at 847-244-1101, ext. *501. SHIP counselors help by appointment with Medicare enrollment, Part D and Medigap, and staff help with Benefit Access, LIHEAP, SNAP and Medicaid applications. (source: https://www.gurnee.il.us/residents/senior-services-information)
Warren Township is at 17801 W. Washington, Gurnee, 847-244-1101, and the Township Assessor's Office is reached at extension 2. (source: https://gurnee.il.us/connect/phone-numbers)

cities.name: Vernon Hills
localNotes: Vernon Hills Village Hall is at 290 Evergreen Drive, 847-367-3700, and the Seniors Center is on its lower level, open Monday through Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and staffed by the Vernon Hills Park District. Membership is for adults 55 and older; the page lists activities and trips and does not mention benefits or Medicare help. (source: https://vernonhills.org/379/Seniors-Center)

Vernon Hills residents are in Libertyville Township north of Route 60 and Vernon Township south of Route 60, so the township assessor depends on the address. The Libertyville Township Assessor is at 359 Merrill Court, Libertyville, 847-362-5900. (source: https://vernonhills.org/366/Community-Resources and https://libertyvilletownship.us/about-us/assessor)

cities.name: Lake Zurich
localNotes: The Ela Township Assessor's Office is at 1155 East IL-22, Lake Zurich, open Monday to Thursday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Staff help with exemptions. (source: https://elatownship.gov/departments/assessor)

Ela Township says senior property tax exemptions require owning and living in the property as a primary residence at age 65 or older, with applications online or through the Assessor at 847-438-8370. Its Senior & Disabled Bus for residents 55 and older or with disabilities is 847-438-6677. (source: https://elatownship.gov/service)

cities.name: McHenry
localNotes: The McHenry Township Senior Center, 3519 North Richmond Road, Johnsburg, 815-344-3555, hosts Senior Services Associates, which gives information and form help on Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and the Benefit Access Program and offers adult protective services and nursing home ombudsman services. (source: https://www.mchenrytownship.com/supervisor/senior-center/)

The McHenry Public Library's senior services page lists the McHenry Township Senior Center as a local service for McHenry residents. The page's map link gives 3703 N. Richmond Road, so confirm the address before visiting. (source: https://mchenrylibrary.org/index.php/11-adults/64-senior-services)
The McHenry Township Assessor's office is open Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm at 815-385-0175 and has an Exemptions page. (source: https://www.mchenrytownship.com)

McHenry County lists a senior homestead exemption of up to $8,000 for age 65 or older and a low-income senior assessment freeze at household income of $75,000 or less, with applications due July 1. The Office of Assessments is 815-334-4290. (source: https://www.mchenrycountyil.gov/departments/assessments/exemptions)
